summary: A reply to David Walden's request in RFC 473 for MIX tools, passed along by UCSB. A graduate student reports having written a MIXAL assembler in SNOBOL4 and a MIX simulator in 360 assembler, with the assembler well debugged but costly to run and the simulator only partly debugged.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC passes along a UCSB student's reply to a request for MIX tools. He reports an assembler and simulator, with different levels of testing and documentation.

subtitle: A UCSB report on a MIXAL assembler and a partly debugged MIX simulator.

tldr.problem: RFC 473 asked whether Network hosts had software for Knuth's MIX computer and its MIXAL assembly language.
tldr.mechanism: A UCSB graduate student reports an assembler written in SNOBOL4 and a simulator written in 360 Assembler, and offers information and source code.
tldr.outcome: The assembler was fairly well debugged and documented; the simulator was only partly debugged and lacked documentation.

sections.title: A Reply About MIX
sections.content:
John Pickens forwards a response to David Walden's question in RFC 473 about MIX and MIXAL tools. The response was written by UCSB graduate student Mark Scott Johnson.

The note directs questions about inexpensive use to Roland F. Bryan at UCSB.
sections.plainLanguage: A UCSB student answers the network's request for MIX software. The RFC passes on his description and contact information.

sections.title: Assembler and Simulator
sections.content:
Johnson says he wrote a MIXAL assembler in SNOBOL4 and a MIX simulator in 360 Assembler. The assembler was fairly well debugged and had documentation, though it was expensive to run.

The simulator was only partly debugged. Instructions other than I/O had been tested somewhat, while disk-file and magnetic-tape simulation were incomplete.
sections.plainLanguage: The assembler was more complete but costly to run. The simulator still needed testing and did not yet support all described features.

sections.title: Offer to Share the Programs
sections.content: Johnson offers to provide the documentation that existed, information about accessing the programs, and their source code. He hoped to finish the simulator in the next quarter and said he would try to maintain and correct the programs if users found bugs.
sections.plainLanguage: The author offered to share the programs and existing instructions. He also invited users to report problems so he could try to fix them.
